question: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.
